summary: kiln-pool pods are shared mutable state — once leased, any pre-existing scripts on the pod (other lab bootstraps, autonomous loops) can also acquire/restart kiln serve, causing mid-eval HTTP 500 / RemoteDisconnected for the new lessee. On this pod, the pi-compaction-grpo v062 autonomous loop's startup script restarted kiln serve mid-iter0-eval and 4/23 tasks errored. There's no isolation mechanism between concurrent agents sharing a pod's filesystem + kiln-serve singleton.
repro_hint: Acquire any kiln-pool H100; ps -ef | grep -i pi-compaction may reveal another lab's bootstrap script still running. The kiln-serve binary itself is a singleton on port 8420 — only one process can bind it.

summary: cuda_grpo_ablation on pi-compaction-sized rollouts is prohibitively slow even with KILN_GRAD_CHECKPOINT_SEGMENTS=8: 4 strong-signal groups × ~30K tokens each = ~120K total token budget; full training step did not produce a single progress= line in 6 minutes on H100 SXM. Pi-doctest training (~150K total token budget over 11 groups) completed in 2-3 min on the same hardware. The 4x slowdown isn't strictly token-count proportional — long-sequence GDN backward pass dominates wall time and scales superlinearly.
repro_hint: Build a GrpoGroup with completions whose combined assistant-text + source-text is ~15-30K tokens each; submit to cuda_grpo_ablation phase1 with rank=16 lr=1e-5 KILN_GRAD_CHECKPOINT_SEGMENTS=8. Pi-doctest training data has ~3K tokens per group total, which is what kiln-train is tuned for.

summary: Shared-prefix reference forward optimization (PR #1055, landed on main) reduces ref-forward work ~n_completions×, but the GRPO policy forward+backward path remains the dominant cost at long context (>7K tokens). Iter 2's strong-signal groups had ~9-11K-token sequences. With KILN_GRAD_CHECKPOINT_SEGMENTS=32, KILN_STREAMING_TILE_TOKENS=512, KILN_SPOOL_CHECKPOINT_BOUNDARIES=1: VRAM fits (12 GB used) but no progress= line in 10 min — CPU-bound at 99% on kernel-launch overhead from many small tiles. With defaults (segments=8, tile=2048): OOM at streaming GDN tile [4096, 6144) of 7719 (tile_size=2048) — DriverError(CUDA_ERROR_OUT_OF_MEMORY) at layer 30. The streaming GDN per-tile transient + checkpoint recompute is the next memory-and-launch-overhead bottleneck.
repro_hint: On H100 80GB CUDA: cuda_grpo_ablation --mode phase1 --rank 16 on GRPO groups with ~10K-token total sequences. Default env: OOMs at streaming GDN tile 2. Aggressive grad-ckpt env: CPU-bound on kernel launches, no progress in 10 min. The fix likely needs (a) larger-but-tile-internally-checkpointed GDN tiles, or (b) fused multi-layer chunked GDN+attn kernels that amortize launch cost across layers.

summary: Long-context GRPO training is now tractable on consumer GPUs (24 GB) at default settings. PR #1056 (trainer/grpo: per-layer tile reverse over multi-layer segments) landed on main. The existing per-layer tile reverse (`exact_gdn_single_layer_tiled_reverse` / `full_attention_single_layer_tiled_mlp_reverse`) had been gated to single-layer segments (`seg_end == seg_start + 1`), so it only fired when `KILN_GRAD_CHECKPOINT_SEGMENTS == num_layers`. Default segments=4 on H100 / 8 on 24 GB / 12 on 16 GB never triggered it. PR #1056 adds a `multi_layer_per_layer_tile_reverse` wrapper that iterates layers inside multi-layer segments and chains gradients layer-to-layer, so the tile path now fires regardless of segment count. Validated end-to-end: iter 2 GRPO step on 3 strong-signal groups (~7700-token sequences) completed in ~17 min on H100 with peak 17 GB VRAM (previously: OOM or 10+ min hang). One-epoch lr=1e-5 produced ~no eval shift (0.314 vs 0.314 baseline) — as expected for very small total update; the win is the pipeline is now functional, not the +composite.
repro_hint: On any GPU with `KILN_DISABLE_FUSED_GDN_GATES=1`: cuda_grpo_ablation --mode phase1 --rank 16 on a GRPO group with multi-layer segments at long context. Pre-#1056: OOM or monolithic-fallback hang. Post-#1056: tile-reverse fires per-layer, training completes.

summary: After GRPO training (iter 2: 3 strong groups, lr=1e-5; iter 3: 1 strong group, lr=1e-3), the trained adapter produces *byte-identical* response text on all 23 eval tasks compared to the base model. mean_composite = 0.31403227054303057 to 17 decimal places matches the base model eval. This holds even with lr=1e-3 (100x the original Phase 1 default). Either the LoRA weights are being applied with effective scale=0, the adapter isn't actually loading despite `/v1/adapters/load` returning `{"status":"loaded"}`, or GRPO's analytic tail produces near-zero gradients at this scale (KL penalty dominates, clipping epsilon swallows the IS ratio update, etc). Needs investigation before further GRPO iterations are meaningful — they're currently no-ops on eval.
repro_hint: Train GRPO with any lr/rank/data, save adapter, load via `/v1/adapters/load`, run eval rollout, diff response text against base. Expected: at least some responses change at lr=1e-3 (a huge LR for LoRA). Actual: zero differences in 23/23 tasks across two independent runs.
